title: Ang 859: Gond begins
hookLine: Guru Ram Das opens the raga
tomorrow: what can you take of a teacher when you leave home?

cards: Tear open a bag of sesame seeds and a few always spill. Nobody chases them across the counter; they're too small to matter.
On ang 859, Guru Ram Das opens raga Gond, and that's the exact seed he picks to say what God never loses.

teach.h: GOND OPENS WITH GURU RAM DAS.
teach.b: Gond's opening hymn, in paraphrase: if in your mind and heart you set your hope on the Lord, you'll receive the fruits your heart longs for.
The Lord knows everything that happens in the soul; of anyone's effort, not even a sesame seed is lost. The word there is til, the sesame seed. So Gond starts small, on purpose.
Not a mountain of good deeds. Not a big win. A til of effort.
An extra shift, a patient answer, a chore nobody thanked you for, a hope set quietly on God. Guru Ram Das says none of it falls off the counter.

teach.h: SET YOUR HOPE ON THE LORD.
teach.b: Then the hymn goes on, in paraphrase: O my mind, set your hope on the Lord, the Master who is present in everyone.
Hope comes first, and the fruit follows. Here's what makes it worth repeating to a friend. The line doesn't say every effort pays off the way you planned.
It says the effort is known. The One who sees what happens inside a person keeps count of what nobody else saw.
That's how Gond opens in the Granth: a new sound, and the smallest seed in the kitchen, kept.

how: Raga Gond's hymns are sung in kirtan like the rest of the Granth; it opens on ang 859 with Guru Ram Das's hymn of hope and the sesame seed of effort.

games.q: your little brother spent an hour on a card for bebe, and she barely glanced at it. he's crushed. what does the hymn on ang 859 say?
o: the effort is known even when it isn't seen; it isn't lost.
next time make it bigger, so she can't miss it.
it doesn't matter; feelings about cards are small stuff.
games.why: Guru Ram Das: the Lord knows what happens in the soul, and not a sesame seed of anyone's effort is lost.

practice: Find one tiny thing: a sesame seed, a grain of rice, a crumb, a bead. Set it in your open palm and look at it for the sit: its size, its color, how little it weighs. Let it stand for one small effort nobody noticed.
If you'd like, read the hymn on ang 859 first.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: til, a sesame seed; 'ik til na gavaaee,' not a sesame seed lost, ang 859.

carryVoice: Gond: a new raga, and a seed of effort God doesn't drop. Small, and kept.
